data.title: Bitcoin slides toward $60,000 as spot ETF outflows near $3 billion
data.description:
Bitcoin is having a rough November. On Thursday, November 19, the largest crypto asset traded at approximately $63,800 after a week that took about 13% off its price.

The slide has put the psychologically important $60,000 mark within view.

Three forces are doing the damage at once: steady money leaving US spot Bitcoin ETFs, a broad sell-off on Wall Street, and growing worry that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates again.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $2.9 billion in net outflows for November through the 18th. That figure covers fewer than three weeks of trading.

The pace picked up toward the end of that stretch. Daily outflows came in at $239.9 million on November 17, then climbed to between $306.4 million and $306.5 million on November 18.

One name stands out. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, ticker IBIT, accounted for approximately 83% to 87% of the month's ETF outflows.

The cumulative result shows up on the balance sheet. Combined net assets across the Bitcoin ETFs fell to $77.7 billion, a three-month low.

The ETF story is not happening in isolation. Crypto losses on Thursday came alongside a wide sell-off in traditional markets, as risk assets broadly lost favor.

Concerns about further Federal Reserve rate hikes are a big part of that mood.

Rising Treasury yields and a strong dollar have piled on. Those conditions helped push Bitcoin to roughly 20% below the average entry prices set during recent institutional purchases.

Intraday action reflected the stress. Bitcoin dipped below $63,000 at points, and earlier in the week it touched a 24-hour low of $62,068.

Another source of supply is coming from inside the industry. Mining companies including Riot and Marathon Digital (MARA) have liquidated assets to fund new AI infrastructure, which has added to selling pressure.

For anyone tracking institutional demand, the ETF data is the most important signal on the board. Nearly $3 billion leaving in under three weeks shows that bridge carries traffic in both directions.

The concentration in IBIT matters as well. When one fund drives the vast majority of redemptions, it points to a specific set of holders reshaping their exposure, rather than a slow drift across the entire market.

The gap between current prices and recent institutional entry points is a second risk. With Bitcoin around 20% below where many large buyers got in, a further decline could test the conviction of those holders and invite more selling.

The $60,000 level is the obvious marker to watch. Daily ETF flow data is the other key indicator. A slowdown in redemptions, or a return to inflows, would be the first sign that institutional demand is stabilizing.

Bitcoin has shed about 13% in a week, institutional buyers are underwater, and the macro backdrop is offering little help.

data.title: Marsh to Highlight How Perspective Drives Performance at the Formula 1® Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix
data.description:
Marsh (), the leading professional services firm in risk, strategy, people, and investments, will have a prominent presence at the Formula 1® Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix as Formula 1's Official Risk Partner and Official Insurance Brokering Partner. During the event, taking place November 19–21, 2026 on the streets of Las Vegas, Marsh will have trackside signage and out of home advertising throughout the street circuit.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix — now in its third year since debuting in 2023 — drew approximately 56 million viewers worldwide last year and runs on the second-longest street circuit in the 2026 season at 6.201 kilometers. The race is one of eight street circuits on the calendar this year, and its Las Vegas Strip setting makes it among the most recognizable events in the global sport.

"The Las Vegas Grand Prix is one of the most watched sporting events on the planet, and it gives us a remarkable stage to bring our clients into the center of that energy," said John Jones, Chief Marketing and Communications Officer at Marsh. "Formula 1 attracts the kind of business leaders we work with every day — people who understand that performance, at its core, is about how you manage risk to seize opportunity and drive results. That's the conversation we're here to have."

The weekend will feature high-level engagement with Marsh, Formula 1 leadership and racing experts. Events include a fireside chat between Michelle Sartain, President of Marsh Risk US and Canada, and Emily Prazer, Chief Commercial Officer of Formula 1 and CEO of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, as well as a discussion between Kate Brennan, Marsh General Counsel, Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, and Chris Medland, Formula 1 journalist and commentator. The events will offer Marsh clients a rare window into the strategic thinking driving one of the world's fastest-growing sports properties, as well as insights into making decisions under pressure and recognizing winning opportunities both on and off the track.

Marsh's presence at Las Vegas is part of its broader activation across the 2026 Formula 1 season, which includes trackside branding at select races and The Risk Perspective, a content series featured on F1.com and the F1 app. The series explores specific circuits where drivers and teams must interpret risk, adapt to evolving conditions, and make decisive calls under pressure — illustrating how perspective turns uncertainty into advantage and insight into performance.

Marsh, across its businesses, has a long history of working closely with leading companies in the automotive, transportation, mobility, sports, and entertainment sectors. The Formula 1 partnership enables Marsh to engage more deeply with clients and industry stakeholders worldwide, showcasing tailored solutions that respond to evolving risks and opportunities.

About Marsh

Marsh () is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

About Formula 1®

Formula 1® racing began in 1950 and is the world’s most prestigious motor racing competition, as well as the world’s most popular annual sporting series. Formula One World Championship Limited is part of Formula 1® and holds the exclusive commercial rights to the FIA Formula One World Championship™. Formula 1® is a subsidiary of Liberty Media Corporation (, FWONK, LLYVA, LLVYK) attributed to the Formula One Group tracking stock. data.title: Anthropic's $81 Bln IPO Highlights AI's Trillion-Dollar Potential
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Anthropic (ANT) has made history with an $81.3 billion initial public offering, becoming the first publicly traded frontier artificial intelligence company and reaching a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.

The maker of the Claude chatbot priced its shares at $83 apiece, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, reflecting strong investor demand.

Its Nasdaq debut on November 19 under the ticker ANT saw shares open at $111.50, approximately 34.3 percent above the IPO price, briefly pushing its market valuation beyond $2 trillion. The offering surpassed SpaceX's $75 billion IPO in June 2026 to become the largest in history.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic has emerged as a major player in the AI industry. Its Claude models power chatbot, coding and enterprise applications, generating revenue through consumption-based services and paid subscriptions.

Revenue surged to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million in 2024. First-half 2026 revenue reached $16.29 billion, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. Meanwhile, its operating loss narrowed to $693 million from $2.14 billion, indicating improving financial performance.

However, sustaining this growth requires substantial investment. Anthropic has committed more than $600 billion in spending with approximately eight partners over a decade, including at least $110 billion with Amazon, $114.5 billion with Google and $44.9 billion with Microsoft. Amazon and Google are also major investors, highlighting the interconnected financial relationships underpinning the AI industry.

Competition from OpenAI, Google, Meta and other AI developers remain intense. Nevertheless, Anthropic has established a strong enterprise presence, accounting for 60.5 percent of AI token spending tracked by Ramp during the week ended October 23.

For investors, Anthropic offers exposure to the rapidly expanding AI market, supported by exceptional revenue growth and increasing enterprise adoption. However, its $1.5 trillion IPO valuation places considerable emphasis on future execution.

Its ability to manage infrastructure costs, maintain its competitive position and translate growing demand into sustainable profits will ultimately determine whether its market valuation is justified.

data.title: Cattle futures rise on tight supplies, technical buying
data.description:
By Karl Plume

Chicago Mercantile Exchange cattle futures rose for a second consecutive day on Thursday, supported by technical buying as tight cattle supplies overshadowed concerns about beef demand.

Feeder cattle futures climbed and live cattle reached a three-week peak after actively-traded nearby contracts broke through technical chart resistance at key moving averages.

Markets were also underpinned by expectations for continued tight supplies ahead of a USDA report due on Friday. Analysts, on average, believe the report will show on-feed cattle supplies as of November 1 slightly below a year ago, and October placements down 3% from last year.

"We're going to tighten the on-feed supply and, for now at least, futures are trying to suggest that's going to more than offset a little consumer demand concern," said Rich Nelson, chief strategist with Allendale.

The wholesale choice boxed beef cutout value fell $2.44 to $353.52 per hundredweight on Thursday, while select cuts dropped $2.48 to $341.97 per cwt, the USDA said.

CME December live cattle rose 3.075 cents to 222.850 cents per pound, while actively-traded February futures gained 3.300 cents to settle at 227.200 cents.

January feeder cattle ended 4.50 cents higher at 335.550 cents per pound.

CME lean hog futures rose on Thursday, lifted by short covering after two sessions of declines that dragged prices to contract lows a day earlier.

However, weak consumer demand for pork remained a headwind for the market.

December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled 1.075 cents higher at 52.425 cents per pound. February hogs (LHG27) ended up 0.900 cent at 58.050 cents a pound.

The wholesale pork carcass cutout value fell 82 cents on Thursday to $68.66 per cwt, just above a six-year low of $68.44 on Tuesday, the USDA said.

Muskoka, Ontario – November 19th, 2026 – TheNewswire – Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (CSE: SCM) (“Steadright” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that it has entered into a Share Acquisition Facilitation and Funding Agreement dated November 13, 2026 (the “Agreement”) with Terracasa Investment & Consulting FZCO (“Terracasa”), a free zone company based in Dubai Silicon Oasis, United Arab Emirates. Under the Agreement, the Company will fund the acquisition of a 20% interest in a private Moroccan company that holds a critical minerals project in southern Morocco. The transaction would add a further asset to Steadright’s growing Moroccan portfolio, which includes interests in the TitanBeach Titanium Project and the Copper Valley Project, as well as a binding MOU for the historic Polymetallic Goundafa Mine.

The Transaction

Terracasa is acting as facilitator for the transaction, drawing on its prior dealings with the target company’s shareholders, from whom the 20% interest is being acquired. Under the Agreement, Steadright will provide the equivalent of CAD 400,000 to fund the acquisition, which will be paid from the Company’s existing cash. The shares are to be registered in the name of NSM Capital Sarl (“NSM”), a Moroccan company owned by Steadright (76.5%) and Critical Foundation Metals Inc. (“CFM”) (23.5%), giving Steadright an effective indirect interest of approximately 15.3% in the target company. The transaction is expected to complete within 30 days, or less. The identities of the target company and the project are being kept confidential at this stage for commercial reasons. The Company expects to provide further details upon completion of the transaction.

Role of the Facilitator

Terracasa will manage the remaining formalities for the acquisition, including coordinating with the Moroccan authorities and the target company’s shareholders to complete registration of the shares in the name of NSM. Terracasa will also provide Steadright with copies of the signed transfer documents, shareholder consents and the updated share register, and will report to the Company in writing every seven days until completion.

Related Party Disclosure

The CEO of Steadright holds an indirect interest of 6% in CFM through a 33% ownership interest in a private entity that owns 18% of the common shares of CFM. In addition, a consultant to the Company, who is the spouse of a former director of Steadright, together with her immediate family, is the controlling shareholder of CFM and owns a majority of CFM common shares.

ABOUT STEADRIGHT CRITICAL MINERALS INC.

Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. is a mineral exploration company established in 2019.

Steadright is focused on acquiring exploration and historical mining projects in the Moroccan critical minerals space that can be advanced toward production.

Steadright currently holds its Moroccan exposure through NSM Capital Sarl, which has a 32% interest in Shang Tang, a Moroccan-based company with over 192 sq. km of mineral exploration claims comprising the TitanBeach Titanium Project, along with the Copper Valley Project. Steadright also has a binding MOU for the historic Goundafa Mine in the Kingdom of Morocco, which is fully permitted for mining operations.

data.title: Bausch + Lomb post-surgical ocular pain asset fails phase 2 main goal
data.description:
Key points:
  • BL1332, a candidate for post-surgical ocular pain from Bausch + Lomb , failed to meet its primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial.
  • At 24 hours, the topical TRPV1 antagonist did not show a statistically significant improvement vs. vehicle in the sum of pain intensity differences in both dose strengths tested (0.30% and 0.15%).
  • Also, a secondary endpoint measuring pain reduction during the first six hours after surgery, the 0.30% dose demonstrated a nominally significant reduction compared to vehicle.
  • "These findings, together with results from a previously reported Phase 1b study of BL1332 in participants with capsaicin-induced pain, will help shape discussions with the FDA and the program's future development," the company said. 
  • The phase 2 trial was evaluating BL1332 in patients with pain after photorefractive keratectomy surgery.

data.title: P&G to Cut Up to 30% of Product-Supply Workers Amid Automation Push
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Procter & Gamble said it plans to cut 20% to 30% of its product-supply jobs by 2030, as it implements more automation into its supply chain.

The consumer goods company said the job cuts, which will include contractors, are part of its ongoing effort to lower supply-chain costs.

P&G expects to deliver $1.8 billion in annual productivity savings by the end of this decade, in part from the workforce reduction, Chief Product Supply Officer Luc Reynaert said during an investor day event Thursday.

Product supply is also becoming more automated, Reynaert said. "Success heavily depends on a workforce with the skills to scale and optimize these technologies," he said.

P&G has been working for several years to improve its supply chain through a program it calls Supply 3.0. The plan involves keeping supply steady, digitizing and automating the supply chain, training its workforce on those new tools, and improving sustainability.

Eventually, P&G is aiming for 90% or greater free cash flow productivity from the improvements.

"Supply 3.0 is not a destination. It is the foundation that will evolve us into the supply chain of the future," Reynaert said.

P&G didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about the job cuts.

data.title: Gap cuts forecast, but signs of Old Navy recovery lift shares
data.description:
By Neil J Kanatt and Danielle Kaye

Gap cut its annual sales and profit forecasts on Thursday after a slower-than-expected start to the holiday quarter, even as improving trends at Old Navy, its largest brand, signaled its turnaround efforts were gaining traction.

Shares of the US apparel retailer rose more than 2% in extended trading after Old Navy posted better-than-expected quarterly sales and the company named Vuori executive Ashley Kechter to lead Athleta, its struggling activewear brand.

Investors have been seeking signs that Old Navy is recovering from a recent slump. While the namesake Gap brand has driven recent growth, the rest of Gap's portfolio — encompassing Old Navy, Athleta and Banana Republic — has lagged.

Gap earlier this year blamed weak sales of dresses and other seasonal categories on merchandising missteps at Old Navy and appointed retail veteran Michael Francis as the banner's chief executive in August.

Old Navy's revenue rose 1% to $2.30 billion in the third quarter, beating analysts' expectations. Gap Chief Executive Richard Dickson said in a statement the banner showed "meaningful sequential improvement."

Gap now expects fiscal 2026 sales to be roughly flat, compared with its previous forecast for growth of 1% to 1.5%. Analysts on average had expected growth of 1.4%, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company lowered its adjusted annual earnings forecast to between $2.29 and $2.34 per share from its prior range of $2.35 to $2.45.

Athleta, Gap's smallest banner by revenue, continues to face pressure as it works through excess inventory and seeks to boost brand desirability. It reported a 15% drop in comparable sales in the third quarter.

For the holiday quarter, the retailer expects sales to range from flat to down 1%, compared with analysts' expectations for a 2.6% increase. The company said the current quarter started slowly before improving in recent weeks.

TJX said this week that holiday demand for discounted merchandise remained strong, but Target reported continued weakness in apparel, particularly in women's fashion.

For the third quarter ended October 31, Gap reported net sales of $4.01 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of about $4.02 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of 82 cents beat expectations of 78 cents.

data.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
data.description:
Bausch + Lomb , said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study.

However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

The contact lens maker said it plans to discuss the results with the US Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial.

Here are some details:

  • The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy, or PRK, a laser procedure used to correct vision

  • US-listed shares of the eye-care company were down 1.4% in extended trading

  • Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases, and there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways, the company said

  • At six hours after surgery, secondary goal of complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two BL1332 doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving placebo

  • The company also said patients treated with BL1332 showed signs of faster healing of the cornea, the eye's outer surface
